messages:
Maya (oncall): Heads-up: getting a bunch of noisy canary alerts for text-gen-api in eu-west-1 since ~02:14 UTC. Alerts are flapping, looks probe-related, not a clear customer error yet.
incident-bot: Created incident INC-2024-318 (pager to oncall). Severity: P2 — Canary failures.
Ethan: I'm awake, grabbing console. Any deploys in the last hour?
Priya: No deploys from infra or app teams in last 2h per deploy-bot. Seems like probe churn.
Jules: Logs show repeated 503s from the probe runner hitting model-host-7, interspersed with OKs. Could be transient network or probe sensitivity.
Maya (oncall): OK let's reduce noise first. Can we silence the pager for the canary alerts for 15m while we triage? Requesting temporary silence for the alert rule.
Ethan: Silencing alert rule: grafana alert id 8421, setting for 15m now.
SRE-runbook-bot: Silence applied: alert 8421 (eu-west text-gen canary) until +15m per request by Ethan.
Priya: Suggest we change the evaluation window to require 3 consecutive failures before alerting. Current rule fires on 1/5 failures -> too chatty.
Jules: I agree. The probe runs every 30s and we have noisy infra; 3 consecutive failures would give ~90s before alert. Fine for early-warning canaries.
Maya (oncall): Also let's look at the probe config: frequency and timeout. If it's 30s with 500ms timeout and backend transient 300ms bursts, that's spiky. Maybe increase timeout or backoff frequency.
Ethan: I'm SSHing into canary-control to inspect job: 
```
kubectl get canaryprobe text-gen-eu-west -o yaml
```
Job shows schedule: interval: 30s, timeout_ms: 400, threshold_latency_ms: 200, retries: 0.
Priya: threshold_latency_ms: 200 is tight for gen workloads at tail latencies. We should bump threshold to 500ms and add retries=1. Also set consecutive_failures_before_alert: 3.
Maya (oncall): Agree. Make the change in staging first, then to prod canaries. Ethan, can you patch the config and roll to canary runner? Provide exact diff in thread.
Ethan: Patching now. Diff I applied (staging):
```
- interval: 30s
- timeout_ms: 400
- threshold_latency_ms: 200
- retries: 0
+ interval: 45s
+ timeout_ms: 750
+ threshold_latency_ms: 500
+ retries: 1
+ consecutive_failures_before_alert: 3
```
Applying rollout to staging canary pool.
Jules: Nice — increasing interval to 45s will cut noise and still be useful. Consider 60s if we see cost/volume issues.
SRE-runbook-bot: Test checklist: 1) Run 10 synthetic checks via runbook-runner; 2) Verify failure count logic; 3) Ensure alert dedupe window 5m.
Priya: Running step 1 now from runbook-runner: `python tools/canary_runner.py --target text-gen-eu-west --count 10`
Priya: Results: 10/10 OK under patched config in staging, median latency 120ms, 95p 430ms. No alerts triggered.
Maya (oncall): Good. What's the plan for prod rollout and dashboard changes?
Ethan: I'm going to patch prod canary config with the same diff and also update grafana alert to use rolling_count(1m) and require sum_over_time(failed[2m]) >= 3. I'll push the alert patch and link to PR.
Jules: Also add a separate panel showing 'consecutive failures' metric and a spike chart for probe latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) for quick triage.
Priya: I'll create the dashboard panel, name it 'Canary: eu-west text-gen health', with panels: last 1h latency heatmap, consecutive failure counter, probe run rate, and host-level network errors.
Maya (oncall): Good. For now we keep pager silence for the 15m window, but we should notify customer-impact channel if any real user-facing errors appear. No evidence of customer errors yet.
incident-bot: Pager silence window expires in 10 minutes.
Ethan: Prod patch applied. Running 20 test probes via orchestrator: `curl -X POST https://canary-api.internal/run?target=text-gen-eu-west&count=20`
Ethan: Test run results: 18 OK, 2 transient timeouts (timeouts at ~650ms) — with retries=1 they resolved; alert did not fire.
Priya: Confirmed alert rule updated in Grafana: expression uses `sum_over_time(probe_failure{target="text-gen-eu-west"}[2m]) >= 3` and contact routing stays to oncall. Dedupe window 5m set.
Maya (oncall): Can we document the exact decision set to the incident ticket and plan a follow-up to evaluate the false positive rate over 48h? We should review after the weekend.
Jules: Created follow-up ticket: SRE-2009 (Investigate EU canary false positives & tune thresholds), linking dashboards and recent logs. Assigned to Priya + Ethan.
Priya: I'll add a dashboard anomaly panel to track monthly false-positive rate and add an automation to post weekly summary to #eng-sre.
Maya (oncall): One more ask: add a deploy-window suppression for canaries during scheduled infra maintenance windows so probes don't trigger during planned infra work.
Ethan: Filed infra config request with ops-schedule: SET canary-suppression windows 02:00-03:00 UTC on Thursdays.
incident-bot: Silence expired: alert 8421 is unsilenced.
Priya: No new alerts after prod change in the last 20m, only expected historical flapping cleared.
Maya (oncall): Great. Marking incident as resolved for now. Will update postmortem with timeline and config diffs. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
SRE-runbook-bot: Incident INC-2024-318 flagged as resolved by Maya. Follow-up ticket: SRE-2009. Postmortem template: `https://wiki.internal/sre/postmortems/SRE-2009`
Ethan: Quick note: we'll monitor for 48h and revert thresholds if we see missed detection. If customer reports come in, we escalate immediately.
Jules: One small ops-optimization: consider moving probe runner to a VPC egress path with lower packet loss for eu-west to reduce flakiness. Adding as a backlog item in SRE-2009.
Maya (oncall): Closing thread — will file final updates in SRE-2009. Thanks everyone.
